test_title: PYST 11: SSC MTS 2022 - English (Held On: 11 May, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

(Hardly did the ink dried on my weekly column, when) one of my readers called me.

options.text: Hardly had the ink dry on last week's column, when
Hardly did the ink dried on last week's column, when
Hardly had the ink dried on last week's column, when

solution:
The correct answer is "**Hardly had the ink dried on last week's column, when**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let us understand the following points:
 
 
• "last week's column" is a better phrase than "my weekly column" for clarity.
 
• When a story is told in the past tense, the adverbials hardly, scarcely, barely and no sooner are often used to emphasize that one event quickly followed another.
 
• **The verb describing the earlier event is usually in the past perfect tense.**
 
 
 
• **The sentence in option 4 uses the correct verb tense (past perfect) to show that the action of the ink drying happened before the action of the reader** **calling.**

Hence, **the correct answer is option 4**.
